title: Injective module sheaves are injective as module presheaves
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be the category of presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules with sheafification left adjoint to the inclusion [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. If $I$ is injective in $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], then the underlying presheaf of $I$ is injective in $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03FB (lemma-injective-module-injective-presheaf), proof via exact sheafification adjunction

proof.text: The module sheafification functor $\#$ is left adjoint to the inclusion of sheaves by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], and it is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact]. Thus the inclusion of $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ into $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is the right adjoint of an exact functor.

source.place: Section Tag 03CX (sheafification of modules on a ringed site)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] to the exact sheafification functor and its inclusion right adjoint. Since $I$ is injective in $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, the inclusion sends it to an injective object of $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, which is precisely the underlying presheaf of $I$.
